podcasts.name: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Early 1990s Prime Time Success
podcast.body: Limblifter was listed as one of the Canadian bands that gained "prime time" exposure in the early 1990s. "The early 90s were pretty amazing with a long list of Canadian bands getting a shot at prime time. We had moist, the watchman, lowest of the low, sons of freedom, grapes of wrath, rhymes with orange, pure Gandarva's limb lifter."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Formation and Early Success
podcast.body: Limblifter was formed as an offshoot band by brothers Ryan and Kurt Dahle, who were previously in Age of Electric. They achieved several hits that extended their presence in the music scene through the early 2000s. "They formed an offshoot band called Limlifter. And they had some hits that extended through the early 2000s."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Lost CanRock Bands of the '90s: Part 1

podcast.title: Lineup Change and Continued Activity
podcast.body: Kurt Dahle left Limblifter to join The New Pornographers, while Ryan Dahle continued with Limblifter. This change illustrates the dynamic nature of band memberships in the Canadian music landscape, with Ryan Dahle remaining active in the project. "Kurt left to join the new pornographers, where Ryan stayed behind in Limlifter."

xref.title: Collaboration with Ryan Dahle and Steve Bays
xref.body: Hawksley Workman is actively involved in a new band named Mounty, alongside Ryan Dahle (Age of Electric, Limblifter) and Steve Bays (Hot Hot Heat). This collaboration signifies his continued presence in the Canadian music scene through new projects. "Ryan Doll was now working with Hoxley Workman and Steve Bayes of Hot Hot Heat in a band called Mounty."

xref.title: Dahle Brothers' Additional Project
xref.body: Static and Stereo was another band formed by the Dahle brothers, Ryan and Kurt, showcasing their prolific musical collaboration beyond Age of Electric and Limblifter. Its mention implies a level of recognition among listeners. "The doll brothers had another band that you might remember called Static and Stereo."

xref.title: Formation of New Band
xref.body: Mounty is a recently formed band comprising Ryan Dahle (from Age of Electric and Limblifter), Hawksley Workman, and Steve Bays (from Hot Hot Heat). This supergroup-like formation brings together talent from several prominent Canadian rock bands. "Ryan Doll was now working with Hoxley Workman and Steve Bayes of Hot Hot Heat in a band called Mounty."

xref.title: Kurt Dahle Joining
xref.body: Kurt Dahle, previously a member of Age of Electric and Limblifter, joined The New Pornographers. This move marked a significant career transition for Dahle into another prominent Canadian musical group. "Kurt left to join the new pornographers."

xref.title: Post-Breakup Member Activities
xref.body: Following Age of Electric's original run, members pursued various projects: the Dahle brothers formed Limblifter, Todd Kerns became the bass player and backup vocalist for Slash in The Conspirators, and three other members joined Matthew Good's backup band. These transitions highlight the interconnectedness of Canadian musicians. "Todd Kerns from Age of Electric has been working as the bass player in Back of Vocalist for Slash, yes, as in Guns and Roses Slash, in his band The Conspirators."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

This highlights ongoing musical connections and new projects among established Canadian artists. "Ryan Doll was now working with Hoxley Workman and Steve Bayes of Hot Hot Heat in a band called Mounty."
